item.text: I’m checking the current implementation again and pushing the refactor a step further, not just renaming things. With a one-file repo, the next useful improvement is separating the reusable utility from the demo entrypoint and tightening the API surface.

I found the next real cleanup point: `PrefixSum` is still doing utility work, formatting, and demo execution in one class. I’m splitting that into a reusable algorithm class plus a tiny demo entrypoint, and I’ll keep behavior verified after the move.

The refactor is in place: `PrefixSum` is now just the algorithm API, and the sample output path lives separately. I’m compiling both classes and running the demo so the change stays behaviorally neutral.

Refactored the code into clearer roles.

[PrefixSum.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/003_prefix_sum_array/PrefixSum.java:1) is now a pure utility class with two focused APIs: `build(...)` for the common case and `buildInto(...)` when the caller wants to reuse an output array. That removes formatting and demo concerns from the algorithm class and makes the core logic more reusable.

[PrefixSumDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/003_prefix_sum_array/PrefixSumDemo.java:1) now owns the sample execution and output formatting. Verification passed with `javac PrefixSum.java PrefixSumDemo.java` and `java PrefixSumDemo`, which still prints `10 30 40 45 60`.
